keyVerseText: And I, behold, I have given with him Aholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan: and in the hearts of all that are wise hearted I have put wisdom, that they may make all that I have commanded thee;
rootMeaning: The name אׇהֳלִיאָב (ʼOhŏlîyʼâb) derives from the Hebrew components אֹהֶל (ʼôhel) meaning 'tent' or 'dwelling,' and אָב (ʼav) meaning 'father.' Literally, it can be understood as 'tent of (his) father,' which evokes the image of a familial dwelling or a protective covering. This root sense enriches the common English gloss by emphasizing not just a name but a connection to home, heritage, and shelter—concepts deeply tied to both physical and spiritual habitation.
usageInScripture: The word אׇהֳלִיאָב appears five times in Scripture, consistently associated with the individual Aholiab, who serves as the chief assistant to Bezaleel in the construction of the tabernacle. The top translations, such as 'and Aholiab' or 'with him Aholiab,' underscore his partnership role in this sacred work. This consistency highlights Aholiab's integral role in the divine craftsmanship of the tabernacle, reflecting a collaborative effort ordained by God.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding אׇהֳלִיאָב as 'Father's tent' enriches our appreciation of God's provision and the sacred space He commands His people to build. Aholiab's skilled craftsmanship in the tabernacle's construction points to the importance of wisdom and giftedness given by God to serve His purposes. This name and role remind believers that God calls and equips individuals to build His dwelling among His people, symbolizing God’s desire to dwell with humanity. It also reflects the broader biblical theme of God’s intimate presence and the community’s responsibility to honor that presence through faithful service.
keyVerseReflection: Exodus 31:6 states, 'And I, behold, I have given with him Aholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan: and in the hearts of all that are wise hearted I have put wisdom, that they may make all that I have commanded thee.' The mention of Aholiab here emphasizes God’s intentional gifting of wisdom and skill to specific individuals for the sacred task of tabernacle construction. The name אׇהֳלִיאָב, with its meaning tied to 'father’s tent,' underscores the divine commissioning of a craftsman to build a dwelling place for God, highlighting the sanctity and purpose behind his work.
